mainTopic: The sources for the maximum height and width of a מבוי entrance: the משכן's courtyard gate, the doorway of the אולם, royal gateways, and the doorway of the היכל
overview: The משנה limits a מבוי entrance to 20 אמות high and 10 אמות wide, and the גמרא is searching for the source of these numbers in the doorways of the מקדש and the משכן. It first rejects one proof that the משכן is called a מקדש and replaces it with the פסוק 'ועשו לי מקדש.' Next it asks why we don't learn from the courtyard gate of the משכן, which seems to be 20 wide and 5 high. It gives two answers: the gate is not called a plain 'doorway,' or the 15 אמות of hangings measure height, not width. The גמרא then challenges רב's claim that רבי יהודה learns from the doorway of the אולם. רבי יהודה's width dispute is found in a ברייתא, but his allowing 50 אמות goes past the אולם's 40. רב חסדא concludes that a ברייתא misled רב, and that רבי יהודה really learns from royal gateways. The גמרא then tests the רבנן's source, the doorway of the היכל. It asks about the היכל's doors (they were only for privacy) and about the צורת הפתח (רב corrected the משנה to read 'he must narrow it'). A new challenge opens at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The קהתים verse refers to the ארון, not the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof from 'the קהתים who carry the מקדש.' That פסוק describes the ארון and the holy vessels, not the משכן structure.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the previous proof that the משכן is called a מקדש. It explains that the פסוק about the קהתים carrying the 'מקדש' is talking about the ארון, not the משכן itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קהתים only carried the holy vessels, like the ארון, the שלחן, and the מנורה. They never carried the משכן structure. So the word 'מקדש' in that פסוק means the holy vessels, and it proves nothing about what the משכן is called.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a discussion. The proof being rejected, 'ונסעו הקהתים נושאי המקדש', was brought on the previous amud. The rejection here is aimed at that proof.

phrases.english: That verse is written about the Ark.
phrases.notes: The קהתים carried the vessels, not the משכן structure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought on the previous amud, from the קהתים verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The specific proof-text from the קהתים verse, not the idea that the משכן is called מקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'מקדש' in that פסוק refers to the ארון and vessels, not the משכן.

steps.title: A better verse: 'Make Me a מקדש'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source showing the משכן is called a מקדש: 'ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from here: 'And let them make Me a מקדש, and I will dwell among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first proof, the גמרא offers a new פסוק. It shows that the משכן itself is called a מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק opens the instructions for building the משכן, so its word 'מקדש' clearly means the משכן structure. This confirms that 'משכן' and 'מקדש' can be used interchangeably. That is why a doorway measurement from one can be applied to the other.
steps.whatToRemember: The משכן is called a מקדש, as the פסוק says 'ועשו לי מקדש.' So the two names refer to the same kind of holy structure.

phrases.english: Rather, it is learned from here:
"And let them make Me a Sanctuary, that I may dwell among them."
phrases.notes: שמות כה:ח, the command to build the משכן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a valid one.
steps.raayaObject: That the משכן is called a מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות כה:ח, 'ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם.'

steps.title: Why not learn the doorway size from the courtyard gate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both רבנן and רבי יהודה. The gate of the courtyard of the משכן was 20 אמות wide and 5 high, so let a doorway of those measurements count as valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both according to the רבנן and according to רבי יהודה, let them learn from the doorway of the gate of the courtyard. It is written: 'The length of the courtyard is 100 אמות, the width 50 by 50, and the height 5 אמות.' It is also written: 'Fifteen אמות of hangings for one side.' And it is written: 'And for the second side, on this side and that side of the courtyard gate, hangings of fifteen אמות.' Just as there, a doorway 5 high and 20 wide counts, so too here, a doorway 5 high and 20 wide should count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. Why do both opinions learn the doorway size from other doorways, instead of from the gate of the courtyard of the משכן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard was 50 אמות wide. Hangings of 15 אמות covered each side of the gate, using up 30 אמות. That leaves a gate 20 אמות wide, and the courtyard walls were 5 אמות high. If this counts as a doorway, then an entrance 20 wide should be allowed. That contradicts the משנה's limit of 10 אמות width.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to the Rabbis and according to רבי יהודה
Just as there, so too here (a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: The 20 אמות width is not stated in the פסוק. The גמרא figures it out: 50 minus 15 minus 15 equals 20.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this question stood, the משנה's rule that a מבוי entrance wider than 10 אמות needs narrowing would lose its source.

phrases.english: Both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Yehuda,
let them derive it from the doorway of the courtyard gate,
as it is written: "The length of the courtyard is one hundred cubits,
and the width fifty by fifty,
and the height five cubits."
And it is written: "Fifteen cubits of hangings for one side,"
and it is written: "And for the second side, on this side and on that side,

phrases.aramaic: לְשַׁעַר הֶחָצֵר קְלָעִים חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה״,
phrases.english: of the courtyard gate, hangings of fifteen cubits."
phrases.notes: Two sides of 15 make 30 of the 50 אמות, which leaves a gate 20 אמות wide.

phrases.english: Just as there, five high by twenty wide counts,
so too here, five high by twenty wide should count!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן וּבֵין לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֵילְפוּ מִפֶּתַח שַׁעַר הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After confirming that the משכן counts as a מקדש, the גמרא asks why a different משכן doorway was not chosen as the model.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבנן and רבי יהודה, who learn the doorway size from other doorways.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The courtyard gate is also a משכן doorway, measuring 20 wide and 5 high. Learning from it would allow a 20-אמה-wide entrance, against the משנה.

steps.title: It is called 'gate doorway,' not a plain doorway
steps.stepSummary: The courtyard entrance is called 'the doorway of the gate of the courtyard,' not simply a 'doorway.' So it cannot define what a plain doorway is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is called 'the doorway of the gate of the courtyard,' but it is not called simply 'a doorway.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The courtyard entrance has a special name, so it does not set the rule for an ordinary doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model for a doorway must be something the תורה calls 'פתח' with no added description. The courtyard entrance is always labeled 'שער החצר,' a gate, which is a different kind of opening. Its measurements therefore do not define a regular פתח.

phrases.english: It is called "the doorway of the gate of the courtyard,"
but a plain "doorway" it is not called.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in naming: a 'gate' is not a plain 'doorway.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any entrance to the משכן area could serve as the model for a doorway.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an opening the תורה calls a plain 'פתח' is the model. The courtyard 'gate' does not qualify.

steps.title: The 15 אמות measure height, not width
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the '15 אמות of hangings' refers to the hangings' height. So we do not actually know the gate was 20 wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: when it is written 'hangings of fifteen אמות for one side,' it is written about their height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same question. It challenges the math behind the question itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that 15 אמות was the width of each set of hangings, leaving 20 for the gate. This answer says the 15 אמות was their height. Since the תורה never gives the width, the gate's width is unknown, and nothing can be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the פסוק that says the courtyard's height was 5 אמות. This answer does not mean the hangings by the gate were taller than the rest of the wall. Steps 6 and 7 explain that the 5 אמות are measured from the top of the 10-אמה מזבח, so all the courtyard hangings were 15 אמות high.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the courtyard gate is not the model for a doorway. (1) It is called a 'gate,' not a plain 'doorway.' (2) The 15 אמות is height, so the gate's width is unknown.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say instead:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי כְתִיב: ״קְלָעִים חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה לַכָּתֵף״ —
phrases.english: when it is written "hangings of fifteen cubits for one side,"
it is written regarding their height.
phrases.notes: So the width, and therefore the gate's width, is not given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: the measurement refers to height, not width.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 15 אמות are widths, leaving a 20-אמה gate.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 15 אמות are heights, so the gate's width is unknown and cannot serve as a model.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The courtyard gate cannot be used to set the maximum doorway size, so the משנה's limits stand.

steps.title: A verse says the hangings were only 5 cubits high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the last answer. That answer said the '15 אמות' of hangings means height. But a פסוק says the height was 5 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its height?! But it is written: 'And the height five cubits'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 5. A פסוק clearly says the courtyard hangings were 5 אמות high, not 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 escaped the challenge by reading '15 אמות' as the height of the קלעים. That cancels the proof that the gate was 20 wide. But if the height was only 5, the '15' must be a width again, and the original challenge comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
Height (the word used in the פסוק)
The cloth hangings that formed the walls of the courtyard

phrases.english: Its height?! But it is written:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised anyone would say the 15 אמות is the height.

phrases.english: 'And the height five cubits'!
phrases.notes: שמות כז:יח, about the courtyard hangings

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer from Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the 15 אמות of hangings refers to height
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly gives the hangings' height as 5 אמות, so 15 cannot be their height.

steps.title: The 5 cubits are measured from the top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The 5 אמות in the פסוק are counted from the edge of the מזבח and up. The מזבח was 10 high, so the hangings were 15 in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse means from the edge of the altar and upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the '5 אמות' in the פסוק is measured from the top edge of the מזבח upward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח was 10 אמות high. The hangings rose 5 more above it, so the total height was 15. That fits the reading that the '15 אמות' is height, and the answer from Step 5 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge (top rim) of the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The two numbers do not contradict each other. 15 is the total height from the ground. 5 is only the part above the 10-אמה מזבח.

phrases.english: That one is from the edge of the altar and upward.
phrases.notes: The מזבח is 10 אמות tall, and these 5 above it make 15 in total.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק (different starting point of measurement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's 5 אמות is the hangings' total height from the ground
steps.terutzMaskana: The 5 אמות is measured from the edge of the מזבח, so the total is 15

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה allow a wide entrance?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the doorway of the אולם, which was 20 אמות wide. Yet in the משנה he does not argue with the rule that an entrance wider than 10 must be narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really learn from the doorway of the אולם? But we learned in the משנה: 'One wider than ten cubits must be narrowed,' and רבי יהודה does not argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about רבי יהודה. If he learns from the doorway of the אולם, he should allow an entrance more than 10 wide. But the משנה shows no argument from him on width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doorway of the אולם was 40 אמות high and 20 wide. רבי יהודה uses it to allow a tall entrance. By the same logic he should allow a wide one, up to 20. His silence in the משנה suggests he agrees that width must be cut down to 10, so maybe the אולם is not really his source.

keyTerms.meaning: The doorway of the entrance hall of the בית המקדש (40 high, 20 wide)
But we learned in the משנה! (opens a challenge from a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם גָּמַר?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda learn from the doorway of the Entrance Hall?
phrases.notes: The אולם doorway was 20 אמות wide

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
'And one wider than ten cubits must narrow it,'
phrases.notes: From our משנה, about the entrance of a מבוי

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם גָּמַר? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the courtyard-gate discussion and turns to the earlier claim that רבי יהודה's source is the doorway of the אולם
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה derives his rule from the doorway of the אולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the אולם is his model, he should also allow 20 אמות of width. Yet the משנה shows him accepting the 10-אמה width limit.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהודה does argue, in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי יהודה does disagree about width. We see it in a ברייתא, where he says an entrance wider than 10 need not be narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He disagrees in a ברייתא. As it was taught: 'One wider than ten cubits must narrow it.' רבי יהודה says: 'He does not need to narrow it.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by bringing a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה openly argues about width too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רבי יהודה's silence in the משנה means he agrees. אביי shows a ברייתא where he clearly says width over 10 is fine. So he stays consistent with the אולם as his source.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, an אמורא who answers here
A תנאי teaching not included in the משנה
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
He does not need to reduce it

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He disagrees in a baraita, as it was taught:
'And one wider than ten cubits must narrow it,'
phrases.notes: The first תנא's view in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'He does not need to narrow it.'
phrases.notes: Up to the 20-אמה width of the אולם doorway

steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing an outside source (ברייתא) that shows the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's silence in the משנה means he agrees width must be narrowed
steps.terutzMaskana: In a ברייתא, רבי יהודה holds width need not be narrowed, so he is consistent with the אולם

steps.title: Then why not argue in the משנה itself?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה disagrees about width, why does the משנה not record that disagreement?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him disagree in our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further on אביי's answer. If רבי יהודה holds this view, the משנה should have shown him arguing about width there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists both rules, one about height and one about width. Yet it shows רבי יהודה arguing only on height. The question is why the משנה would leave out his view on width.

phrases.english: Then let him disagree in our Mishnah?

steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה, given אביי's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה disputes the width rule, the משנה should have recorded his dispute next to that rule.

steps.title: His argument about height covers width too
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבי יהודה argues about height. The same view applies to width as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He disagrees about the height, and the same is true for the width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's words in the משנה, 'he does not need to reduce,' are said about height but also cover width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows his dispute only once, next to the height rule. His reason, learning from the אולם doorway, applies equally to width. So the משנה did not need to repeat his view, and the ברייתא simply spells it out.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה allows an entrance higher than 20 and wider than 10. The משנה shows only the height dispute, but his view covers width too, as the ברייתא states. The claim that his source is the doorway of the אולם is challenged next and rejected in Step 14.

phrases.english: He disagrees regarding its height,
and the same applies to its width.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the scope of a stated dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's dispute in the משנה is limited to height
steps.terutzMaskana: His dispute about height in the משנה applies equally to width

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה allowing up to 40, 50, or even 100 אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whether רבי יהודה really learns from the doorway of the אולם. A ברייתא quotes him allowing a beam up to 40 and 50 אמות high, and בר קפרא's version says up to 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still: did רבי יהודה really learn from the doorway of the אולם? A ברייתא teaches that if a מבוי's beam is higher than 20 אמות, it must be lowered, but רבי יהודה allows it up to 40 and 50 אמות. And בר קפרא taught that he allows it up to 100.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against the idea that רבי יהודה learns from the doorway of the אולם. It quotes a ברייתא with numbers that seem too big for that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doorway of the אולם was 40 אמות high. Yet this ברייתא has רבי יהודה allowing 50, and בר קפרא's version says 100. These numbers go past the height of the אולם, so the source רב suggested looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And still / and yet: opens a further challenge
An alleyway that opens onto the public domain
He must lower it (reduce the height)
The doorway of the Entrance Hall of the בית המקדש (40 אמות high, 20 wide)

phrases.english: And still,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם גָּמַר?
phrases.english: does Rabbi Yehuda learn from the doorway of the Entrance Hall?
phrases.notes: This repeats רב's claim in order to attack it.

phrases.english: But was it not taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה יְמַעֵט,
phrases.english: An alleyway (whose beam) is higher than twenty cubits must lower it,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר עַד אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda allows it up to forty and fifty cubits.
And bar Kappara taught: up to a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם גָּמַר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Width and height have been settled, so the גמרא now attacks the source itself (the doorway of the אולם).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that רבי יהודה learns from the doorway of the אולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives רבי יהודה heights (50, 100) that go beyond the 40-אמה doorway of the אולם.

steps.title: 100 can be an exaggeration, but 50 cannot be explained
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא's 100 can be read as an exaggeration. But according to רב, 40 comes from the אולם, so where does 50 come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for בר קפרא: 100 is just an exaggeration. But according to רב יהודה (quoting רב), what exaggeration is there? We can understand that רבי יהודה gets 40 from the doorway of the אולם. But where does he get 50 from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its challenge. It first sets aside the number 100, then shows that the number 50 still has no source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A round number like 100 can be a figure of speech meaning 'very high.' But a list of '40 and 50' sounds exact, so it cannot be brushed off that way. The doorway of the אולם explains 40 and nothing more, so 50 shows that רבי יהודה must have a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (sets up a contrast)
An exaggeration, not an exact number
From where does he learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה (the תנא in the ברייתא) with רב יהודה (the אמורא who quoted רב's claim). 'לרב יהודה' means: according to the explanation רב יהודה gave in רב's name.

phrases.english: Granted, according to bar Kappara, it is an exaggeration.
But according to Rav Yehuda, what exaggeration is there?
phrases.notes: רב יהודה quoted רב as saying רבי יהודה learns from the אולם.

phrases.english: Granted, for Rabbi Yehuda, forty —
he learns from the doorway of the Entrance Hall,
but fifty, from where does he get it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְבַר קַפָּרָא גּוּזְמָא. אֶלָּא לְרַב יְהוּדָה מַאי גּוּזְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge of step 12 down to the number 50, which cannot be explained away.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the doorway of the אולם is רבי יהודה's source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A precise number of 50 goes beyond the 40-אמה doorway of the אולם, so the אולם cannot be the source.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a ברייתא misled רב, and רבי יהודה really learns from royal gateways
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא admits the challenge. רב was misled by a ברייתא that ties the רבנן's 20 אמות to the doorway of the היכל. In truth, רבי יהודה learns from the doorways of kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this ברייתא misled רב. It teaches that a מבוי beam higher than 20 אמות, which is higher than the doorway of the היכל, must be lowered. רב reasoned: since the רבנן learn from the doorway of the היכל, רבי יהודה must learn from the doorway of the אולם. But that is not so. רבי יהודה learns from the doorways of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא accepts that רב was wrong. He explains what led רב to his mistake and then gives רבי יהודה's real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא linked the רבנן's 20 אמות to the doorway of the היכל. So רב assumed that רבי יהודה, the one who argues, used the next doorway in the מקדש, the אולם. רב חסדא says רבי יהודה's source is royal gateways instead. Kings built very tall entrances, which explains heights like 50 and more.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary of the בית המקדש (its doorway was 20 אמות high)
But it is not so (rejects the view just stated)
The gateway of kings: very tall royal entrances

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the רבנן learn from the doorway of the היכל (20 אמות), and רבי יהודה learns from royal gateways. רב's idea that the source is the אולם is rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the measurements of a מבוי entrance are based on real model doorways. Each side's measurement depends on which model doorway it uses.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מַתְנִיתָא אַטְעִיתֵיהּ לְרַב,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: this ברייתא misled Rav,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה,
phrases.english: as it was taught: An alleyway that is higher than twenty cubits,
higher than the doorway of the Sanctuary, must lower it.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סָבַר: מִדְּרַבָּנַן מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכַל גָּמְרִי,
phrases.english: He (Rav) reasoned: since the Rabbis learn from the doorway of the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם גָּמַר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda learns from the doorway of the Entrance Hall.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הִיא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִפִּתְחָא דְמַלְכִין גָּמַר.
phrases.english: But it is not so: Rabbi Yehuda learns from the gateway of kings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מַתְנִיתָא אַטְעִיתֵיהּ לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 12 and 13 by accepting the challenge and replacing רבי יהודה's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the challenge, explains where the mistake came from, and gives a new source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה learns from the doorway of the אולם (רב's view, based on the היכל ברייתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה learns from royal gateways, which can be 50 אמות or more high

steps.title: If the רבנן learn from the היכל, a מבוי should need doors
steps.stepSummary: The היכל had doors. So if the רבנן learn from it, they should require doors for a מבוי. But the משנה says only a לחי and/or a קורה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: if they learn from the doorway of the היכל, they should require doors like the היכל had. Why, then, does the משנה teach about making a מבוי fit: בית שמאי say a לחי and a קורה, and בית הלל say a לחי or a קורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the רבנן and challenges their source, the doorway of the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the היכל's doorway is the model, the model should apply all the way and include its doors. Yet the משנה requires no doors at all, even according to the stricter view of בית שמאי. This suggests the היכל is not a full model for a מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Making an alleyway fit for carrying
A side post at the alleyway's entrance
A cross beam over the alleyway's entrance

steps.confusionAlert: Even בית שמאי, who are stricter, require only a לחי and a קורה, not doors. That is what makes the challenge strong.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, אִי מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל גְּמִירִי —
phrases.english: And the Rabbis, if they learn from the doorway of the Sanctuary —
let them require doors, like the Sanctuary,
why then did we learn: making an alleyway fit,
Beit Shammai say: a side post and a cross beam,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה!
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: a side post or a cross beam!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אִי מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל גְּמִירִי — לִיבְעוֹ דְּלָתוֹת כְּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבי יהודה's source, the גמרא challenges the רבנן's source (the היכל) mentioned in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of the doorway of the היכל as the model for a מבוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the היכל is the model, its doors should also be required. But the משנה requires only a לחי and/or a קורה.

steps.title: The doors of the היכל were only for privacy
steps.stepSummary: The doors of the היכל were not what made it an entrance. They were only there for privacy, so a מבוי does not need doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: The doors of the היכל were made only for privacy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 15. The doors of the היכל were only for privacy, so we do not copy them for a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if the רבנן learn from the היכל, why not require doors too? The answer splits the היכל into two parts. The doorway itself is the model, and the doors were only an extra for privacy. So the 'learning' from the היכל applies only to the size of the entrance, not to its doors.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The doors of the Sanctuary
merely for privacy
is what they were made for.
phrases.notes: The doors were not part of what made the היכל an entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּלְתוֹת הֵיכָל לִצְנִיעוּת בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דַּעֲבִידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15 about the doors of the היכל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which features of the source are learned from it: only the opening, not the doors.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the היכל is the model for a מבוי, every feature of it, including doors, should be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doors were only for privacy and are not part of the model. Only the entrance's size is learned.

steps.title: The היכל had a doorway frame yet was only ten אמות wide
steps.stepSummary: If the היכל is the model, then a צורת הפתח should not help an entrance wider than 10 אמות. The היכל had a doorway frame and was still only 10 אמות wide. Yet the משנה says a צורת הפתח works even when the entrance is wider than 10 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a doorway frame should not help, because the היכל had a doorway frame and even so it was only 10 אמות wide. Why then did we learn in the משנה: 'If it has a doorway frame, even if it is wider than 10 אמות, he does not need to narrow it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against using the היכל as the model. It compares the היכל's size with the משנה's rule about a צורת הפתח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היכל's doorway was 20 אמות high but only 10 אמות wide, and it had a צורת הפתח. If the היכל sets the rules, a doorway frame should only be good up to 10 אמות wide. But the משנה allows a צורת הפתח on an entrance wider than 10 אמות, which seems to go against the היכל model.

keyTerms.meaning: The form of a doorway: two side posts with a beam across the top
Ten אמות, the width of the היכל's doorway
To narrow, to reduce the width

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up height and width here. The 20 אמות is the height limit for the beam. This question is about width: the היכל's doorway was 10 אמות wide.

phrases.english: But now, if so,
the form of a doorway should not help it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא הֵיכַל צוּרַת הַפֶּתַח הָוְיָא לוֹ,
phrases.english: for the Sanctuary had the form of a doorway,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת הוּא דִּרְוִיח.
phrases.english: and even so, it was only ten cubits wide.
Why then did we learn:
If it has the form of a doorway,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָחָב מֵעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת —
phrases.english: even though it is wider than ten cubits,
he does not need to narrow it!
phrases.notes: This is the wording of the משנה that the challenge is based on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לָא תַּיהֲנֵי לֵיהּ צוּרַת הַפֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the doors question is answered, a new challenge is raised about width and the צורת הפתח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן's measurements come from the היכל, as checked against the משנה's rule about צורת הפתח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The היכל had a doorway frame and was only 10 wide. So a doorway frame should be limited to 10 wide. But the משנה allows wider, which contradicts the היכל model.

steps.title: רב himself corrected the משנה to say 'he must narrow it'
steps.stepSummary: The question only applies to רב, who learns from the היכל. But רב himself changed the wording of the משנה to 'he must narrow it,' so for him there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this the reason according to anyone except רב? But רב יהודה taught חייא בר רב in front of רב: 'he does not need to narrow it.' And רב told him: teach it as 'he needs to narrow it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The idea that the רבנן learn from the היכל is only רב's explanation, and רב had a different version of the משנה that fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only hurts the view that the היכל is the model, which is רב's view. A story shows that רב corrected the משנה's text from 'he does not need to narrow it' to 'he needs to narrow it.' So for רב, a צורת הפתח does not help past 10 אמות, which matches the היכל exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this the reason according to anyone except…? Used to show a question only applies to one opinion
Teach it (this way), a correction of the text

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a teacher's own version of the text can protect his view from a question. Here רב's reading of the משנה fits his idea about the היכל.

phrases.english: Is this the reason for anyone except Rav?

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב
phrases.english: But Rav Yehuda was teaching Chiyya bar Rav
in front of Rav:
He does not need to narrow it.
And Rav said to him:
Teach it as: 'He needs to narrow it.'
phrases.notes: רב changes the wording of the משנה to match the היכל model.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the text: רב reads the משנה as 'he needs to narrow it.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says a צורת הפתח works even past 10 אמות, which goes against the היכל model.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב, the משנה reads 'he needs to narrow it,' so a צורת הפתח does not help past 10 אמות, just like the היכל.

steps.title: Opening words of a new challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another challenge with 'but if so.' The rest continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is opening a new challenge against the היכל model, and the details come in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'but if so' means: if we accept what was just said, here is a new problem. Nothing is decided yet. Just know that another question about learning from the היכל is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so. Opens a challenge based on what was just accepted

phrases.english: But now, if so,
phrases.notes: The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 18's answer, the גמרא starts a new challenge to the היכל-based view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the רבנן's rules come from the doorway of the היכל (continued on the next amud)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup formula only. The full logic of the attack appears on the next amud.
